title: Logical Puzzles and Arrangements

steps.title: Turn clues into constraints
steps.content: A seating or ordering puzzle gives relationships that must all hold. Translate words such as before, after, immediately next to, left of and between into constraints before choosing an arrangement.
steps.example: If A is before B and B is before C, the order must be A–B–C.

steps.title: Apply an ordering clue
steps.prompt: A is before B. B is before C. Which order is possible?
steps.explanation: Both constraints are satisfied only by A before B before C.
hints: Convert 'A is before B' into a position constraint.
Check each answer option against both constraints, not only one.

steps.title: Use a table or slots
steps.content: For position puzzles, draw numbered slots. For assignment puzzles, make a grid with people on one axis and attributes on the other. Mark confirmed facts and eliminate impossible combinations.
steps.tip: Do not keep the whole puzzle in your head. Write every fixed constraint.

steps.title: Place the middle person
steps.prompt: Four people P, Q, R and S sit in a row. P is left of Q, R is right of Q, and S is left of P. Who is second from the left?
steps.explanation: The only order satisfying all clues is S–P–Q–R. P is second from the left.
hints: Write the four people into numbered slots from left to right.
Apply the left/right constraints in sequence and see which slot remains for each person.

steps.title: Check every clue
steps.content: A candidate arrangement is valid only if it satisfies every statement. If two arrangements remain possible, do not claim a conclusion that is true in only one of them.

questions.prompt: A is taller than B. B is taller than C. Who is shortest?
questions.explanation: A > B > C, so C is shortest.

questions.prompt: Four tasks W, X, Y, Z are ordered. W is before X, X before Y and Y before Z. Which is first?
In a row of five people, the middle position is:
questions.explanation: The third position is the middle of five positions.

questions.prompt: A is immediately left of B. Which pair order is fixed?
options: A and B must be at the ends
questions.explanation: Immediately left means A is directly before B in the row.

questions.prompt: If two arrangements satisfy all given clues, what can you conclude about an extra statement true in only one arrangement?
questions.explanation: A conclusion must hold in every valid arrangement; one counterexample is enough to show it is not guaranteed.

learning_objectives: Translate ordering and seating clues into constraints.
Use slots and tables to track possible arrangements.
Eliminate candidates that violate any clue.
Identify conclusions that hold across all valid arrangements.

common_misconceptions.misconception: One arrangement that satisfies the clues is automatically unique.
common_misconceptions.correction: Check whether another arrangement also satisfies every clue.

common_misconceptions.misconception: Immediately left and somewhere left mean the same thing.
common_misconceptions.correction: Immediately left means adjacent; somewhere left allows intervening positions.

common_misconceptions.misconception: A conclusion can be accepted if most clues support it.
common_misconceptions.correction: Every clue must hold for an arrangement to be valid.

worked_examples.title: Linear seating
worked_examples.input: A, B, C sit in a row. A is left of B; C is right of B.
trace: The only order is A, B, C.
worked_examples.explanation: Convert each sentence into an ordering constraint.

worked_examples.title: Use elimination
worked_examples.input: A task is on Monday, Tuesday or Wednesday. It is not Monday and occurs before Wednesday.
trace: Remove Monday using the first clue.
Before Wednesday leaves Monday or Tuesday.
worked_examples.explanation: Apply each clue to shrink the set of possible answers.

worked_examples.title: Check a syllogism
worked_examples.input: All roses are flowers. Some flowers fade quickly.
trace: Every rose belongs to the flower group.
The fading subset is only some flowers.
No premise says roses are in that subset.
worked_examples.output: Cannot conclude that some roses fade quickly
worked_examples.explanation: Do not assume overlap between groups unless the premises establish it.

company_applications.practice: Use slots and eliminate options that violate any clue.
Separate adjacency clues from general ordering clues.
Check whether the proposed answer is true in every valid case.

srs_cards.question: What are the key ideas in Logical Puzzles and Arrangements?
srs_cards.answer: Translate clues into constraints. Eliminate impossible arrangements systematically. Distinguish necessary conclusions from assumptions. Use tables or diagrams to track relationships.

srs_cards.question: Name a common mistake in Logical Puzzles and Arrangements.
srs_cards.answer: Check every clue and test whether another arrangement also satisfies them.

srs_cards.question: What should you do first in an arrangement puzzle?
srs_cards.answer: Translate each sentence into an explicit position or adjacency constraint.

srs_cards.question: What does immediately left mean?
srs_cards.answer: The person or item is directly adjacent on the left, with no intervening position.

quest.story: A hiring team gives you ordering clues about people, tasks and schedules. The correct answer must satisfy every clue—not just the first one that looks useful.
quest.mission: Turn words into constraints, maintain possible slots and verify every candidate arrangement.
success_criteria: Use numbered slots or a table.
Distinguish forced facts from one possible arrangement.
